leagues.name: LIV Golf League
notes: Owned and funded by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund since the 2022 launch. On 2026-04-30 PIF said the 'substantial investment required is no longer consistent' with its strategy and that it will stop funding the league at the end of the 2026 season; reported spend c. $5bn to date, c. $6bn by year-end; PIF governor and LIV chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan expected to step down (Sky Sports, 2026-04-30, https://www.skysports.com/golf/news/12176/13538273/). In August 2026 LIV announced an unnamed lead investor has signed for 2027, with players set to become majority equity holders ('LIV Golf 2.0', seasons through 2030 affirmed) (livgolf.com news, fetched 2026-09-25). Show 2026 as PIF-owned and flag the change.

13 four-player teams plus wild cards (57 players); 2026 was the first 72-hole no-cut season. 12 events played Feb-Aug 2026 (livgolf.com/schedule, fetched 2026-09-25). LIV Golf Louisiana (June 25-28) was postponed and does not appear on the finished schedule (Sky Sports 2026-04-30). The season-ending Aramco LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship (Aug 27-30, The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort) was cancelled on 2026-08-17; Indianapolis became the finale (Sky Sports, https://www.skysports.com/golf/news/12176/13574162/...). LIV says 2027 will be a 10-event schedule.

League partners (livgolf.com/partners, fetched 2026-09-25): Global Partners Aramco, HSBC ('Global Pillar Partner'), Maaden, Riyadh Air, Roshn Group, Salesforce; Premium Partner Bahri; Presenting Partner JCB; Official Suppliers Arena, Corpay, DAOU, Fever, New Era, Panini, Select Event Group, Trackman; Destination Partners Government of South Australia, Hong Kong Tourism Board, Louisiana Economic Development, Andalucia Tourism. Event names carry the sponsor: ROSHN Group LIV Golf Riyadh (Feb 4-7), MAADEN LIV Golf Virginia (May 7-10).

Team partner lists come from each team's page on livgolf.com (all fetched 2026-09-25); shirt-level placement on team apparel is not documented there, so kits carry placement 'partner' and sponsorsComplete false.

claims.text: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has bankrolled LIV Golf since its 2022 launch and said on 30 April 2026 that the 'substantial investment required is no longer consistent' with its strategy and that it will stop funding the league at the end of the 2026 season; reported spend is c. $5bn to date, rising to c. $6bn by the end of 2026, and PIF governor and LIV chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan is expected to step down.
claims.short: PIF has funded LIV Golf since 2022 and is ending its funding after the 2026 season (c. $5-6bn reported spend).

source.name: Sky Sports

claims.text: In August 2026 LIV Golf announced an agreement with an unnamed lead investor that will 'carry and fund' the league from 2027, with players set to become majority equity holders ('LIV Golf 2.0') and seasons through 2030 affirmed; the investor's identity and terms were not disclosed.
claims.short: LIV Golf's unnamed 2027 lead investor and planned player majority ownership (announced August 2026).

source.name: LIV Golf - LIV Golf reaches agreement with lead investor for its next era

claims.text: ROSHN Group describes itself as 'Saudi Arabia's leading multi-asset class real estate developer and a Public Investment Fund (PIF company)' in its own press release naming it Title Partner of LIV Golf Riyadh 2026.
claims.short: ROSHN is a PIF company (its own press release).

source.name: ROSHN Group press release

claims.text: The Public Investment Fund holds a 22.55 percent stake in Bahri (National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia) and 20 percent is held by Saudi Aramco Development Company, with the remainder in public shares.
claims.short: PIF holds 22.55% of Bahri; Saudi Aramco Development Company holds 20%.

source.name: AGBI (Arab Gulf Business Insight) company profile

claims.text: LIV Golf confirmed on 17 August 2026 that the Aramco LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship (Aug 27-30, The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort) 'will not take place', making Indianapolis the 2026 season finale - weeks after PIF said it would stop funding the league at season's end.
claims.short: LIV cancelled the Aramco Team Championship in Michigan in August 2026.

source.name: Sky Sports

proposedRatings.reasoning: PIF is LIV Golf's owner and sole major funder since 2022 (c. $5-6bn reported spend), so the league itself is Saudi state money. PIF is chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; the state's record (345 executions in 2024, Khashoggi assessment) and the league's explicit sportswashing role make this serious, with the Sky Sports exit claim flagging that funding ends after 2026.

ROSHN describes itself as 'a PIF company', so it is the same Saudi state money as Riyadh Air (already serious in the corpus), amplified here as title partner of the season-opening Riyadh event and a global partner running the ROSHN Rising Stars programme.

Saudi state-linked (PIF 22.55%, Saudi Aramco Development Company 20% per AGBI) but minority holdings without control, so a step below the state-owned sponsors; as a Premium Partner of LIV it still carries Vision 2030 state branding.

Already rated serious in the corpus and the rating carries over: the Saudi state owns 81.48% of Aramco directly plus 16% via PIF, and Aramco is a LIV Golf Global Partner and was title partner of the (cancelled) Team Championship.
Already rated serious in the corpus: Ma'aden is ~67% PIF-owned, and at LIV it is a global partner and title partner of MAADEN LIV Golf Virginia, so the same state link applies.
Already rated serious in the corpus (PIF-owned national carrier with drafted why-text); at LIV it is a Global Partner, so the existing rating carries over unchanged.

HSBC Holdings plc is listed in London, Hong Kong and New York with no state shareholder disclosed on its investor site; a 'none' tier matches the corpus treatment of other non-state-listed sponsors, though a person decides.

LIV Golf 2027 lead investor: unnamed in LIV's August 2026 announcement; identity, terms and finalisation date not disclosed (https://www.livgolf.com/news/liv-golf-reaches-agreement-with-lead-investor-for-its-next-era, fetched 2026-09-25).
PIF spend figures (c. $5bn to date, c. $6bn by end-2026) are attributed by Sky Sports (2026-04-30) to Money in Sport; no primary filing located.
League deal values: no contract values for any LIV partnership are published on livgolf.com; all deals filed with value null.

Partner deal start dates: livgolf.com/partners gives no term dates for Aramco, HSBC, Riyadh Air, Salesforce, Bahri or JCB; only Ma'aden (global partner since 2025) and ROSHN (2025 involvement, title partner from 2026-01-05 release) have dates.
PLUS (Korean Golf Club partner): logo image has no hyperlink and the brand behind it is unconfirmed (livgolf.com/korean-golf-club, fetched 2026-09-25).
Amazing CRE: linked to a sokimnewyork.com collection page; the corporate identity behind the brand was not verified.
New Era current ownership: neweracap.com history page describes four generations of the Koch family but does not state the present ownership structure.
JCB ownership: jcb.com does not state whether JC Bamford Excavators Ltd is family-owned; the Bamford family connection is unconfirmed this pass.

Bahri ownership percentages (PIF 22.55%, Aramco Development Company 20%) come from the AGBI company profile; Bahri's own investor-relations pages (bahri.sa, investors.bahri.sa) do not publish a shareholder breakdown, so a primary filing (Tadawul/annual report) should confirm.

LIV Golf Louisiana (June 25-28, 2026) was postponed per Sky Sports (2026-04-30) and does not appear on the finished livgolf.com/schedule; the cancellation/postponement outcome was not separately confirmed.

Wild-card players (Scott Vincent, Richard T. Lee, Yosuke Asaji, Bjorn Hellgren, Danny Lee, Miguel Tabuena per livgolf.com/teams) have no team and no kit entry; player-level personal sponsors were out of scope this pass.

Destination Partners on livgolf.com/partners (Government of South Australia, Hong Kong Tourism Board, Louisiana Economic Development, Andalucia Tourism) were noted in league notes but not filed as sponsors/deals this pass.

Official Suppliers on livgolf.com/partners beyond those already in the corpus (Arena, Trackman, Select Event Group filed; Corpay, Panini, DAOU, Fever, New Era reused) - Arena/Trackman/Select Event Group owner chains not researched.
HSBC 'Global Pillar Partner' designation appears only on livgolf.com/partners; no HSBC-side press release located to confirm the tier.
